aria: Animated recap of the Cavaliers' 128 to 119 home win over the Pacers: James Harden's 3-pointer with 57 seconds left that made it 124 to 113, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Harden's 51 points, the top scorers, how the Cavaliers won, and Monday's game at the Bulls.

notes: Box score from the Cleveland Cavaliers' 128–119 home win over the Indiana Pacers on Nov 20, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with the final and line score checked against the SI scoreboard and game details from the Associated Press (via ABC News and AOL), Field Level Media, Cavaliers OnSI and Cleveland.com (via Yahoo Sports). All 128 Cleveland points and all 119 Indiana points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores (29–33–43–23 to 29–32–22–36) add up to both totals: 62–61 Cleveland at the half and 105–83 after three. Team totals (threes 19 of 44 to 14 of 34, rebounds 41–50, steals 9–6), points in the paint (48–52) and the biggest leads (Cleveland 24, Indiana 14) are from the Covers.com box score; the 24-point lead came at 107–83 early in the fourth quarter (SI play-by-play; Field Level Media). Third- and fourth-quarter points are from the line score. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Friday's games.

Indiana led by 14 in the first half, 50–36 (SI play-by-play; Field Level Media), before a 19–5 Cleveland run (Field Level Media). Tied 74–73 Cleveland about four minutes into the third, the Cavaliers then went on a 21–4 run in which Harden scored 13 (AP), and Harden scored 18 in the third quarter (Yahoo/Cleveland.com quarter splits: 15, 9, 18, 9). Indiana cut a 113–90 deficit to two possessions with 2:03 left (AP); Donovan Mitchell's driving floater off a Peyton Watson pass at 1:41 ended the run (SI play-by-play; AP), and Harden scored seven of Cleveland's final nine points (Cleveland.com). Harden had 51 points on 15-of-26 shooting, 7 of 11 from three and 14 of 14 at the line, with 6 rebounds and 6 assists in 40 minutes (box score). It was his 26th career 50-point game, moving him past Kobe Bryant into third behind Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan (AP; Field Level Media), his season high and his high as a Cavalier (AP). Watson returned after missing Wednesday's game with a lower-back contusion (AP). Cleveland has won three of its last four (AP) and went 3–1 on its four-game homestand (Field Level Media); Indiana has lost three straight (AP). Cleveland plays at Chicago on Monday and Indiana at New York on Sunday (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of James Harden's 3-pointer off a pass from Sam Merrill with 57 seconds left in the fourth quarter that made it 124–113, his seventh three of the game (SI play-by-play gives the clock, the assist and the score; Cavaliers OnSI says he 'hit his seventh 3-pointer with 58 seconds left, pushing the lead to 124-113'). He reached 50 points at the free-throw line at 0:42 (Field Level Media). The stories don't describe where the shot came from, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up three. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Cleveland Cavaliers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to James Harden's listed 6-foot-5 and 220 pounds with No. 1 (RealGM; Land of Basketball); no wingspan from a sourced measurement was found, so his arms use the standard proportion. He is drawn in Cleveland's home white with the default figure (no look on the look sheet yet). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
